hero.lead: A nation of 12.3 million that repays its debts on time and finances itself at home, with public debt of 82.2% of GDP in 2025 and a $500 million Afreximbank loan in June 2026.

stats.label: Rate negotiated on the Afreximbank loan, from 9%

capital.heading: Paid on time, financed at home.

record.text: Afreximbank term loan to the Central Bank of Tunisia for the Ministry of Finance, signed June 2026
Public debt, share of GDP, 2025, down from 84.9% in 2024
Interest rate on the Afreximbank loan after negotiation, from 9%
Interest-free central bank facility in the draft 2027 budget, the fourth year running
World Bank financing for drinking and irrigation water, approved 31 March 2026: phase 1 of the Tunisia Water Security and Resilience Program, a US$700 million envelope over 10 years

register.name: Central bank interest-free facility, 2027
register.detail: Central Bank of Tunisia · Draft 2027 budget
register.note: Interest-free, the fourth year running
register.text: Direct financing of the budget by the central bank, about $3.3 billion, proposed in the draft 2027 budget. It is the fourth year running that the budget relies on an interest-free central bank facility.

register.name: Potable Water Security and Resilience Project (P514340)
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 31 March 2026 · phase 1 of the Tunisia Water Security and Resilience Program, US$700 million over 10 years · SONEDE
register.note: 2.3 million people expected to benefit
register.text: Improves the quality and resilience of drinking water services and strengthens the national water utility, SONEDE. It expands the Zarat seawater desalination plant in Gabès from 50,000 to 100,000 cubic metres a day. It serves the water standard, where 65% of Tunisians have safely managed drinking water.

register.name: Irrigation Water Security, Resilience and Value-Addition Project (P511719)
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 31 March 2026 · phase 1 of the Tunisia Water Security and Resilience Program · Jendouba, Béja, Bizerte and Siliana
register.note: Nearly 4,000 farmers expected to benefit directly
register.text: Aims to improve irrigation water services, rehabilitating key irrigation infrastructure in the governorates of Jendouba, Béja, Bizerte and Siliana. It serves the food and livelihood standards, where 24.2% of Tunisians are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Tunisia Social Development Promotion Support Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · Additional financing approved by the Board, release of 27 March 2026 · builds on the original $700 million project
register.note: Family allowances for about 450,000 children aged 6 to 18
register.text: Expands family allowances to approximately 450,000 children aged 6 to 18 from poor and low-income households, and supports the establishment of a national disability fund. It serves the livelihood and education standards, where 16.6% of Tunisians live below the national poverty line.

register.name: Tunisia Energy Reliability, Efficiency, and Governance Improvement Program (TEREG)
register.detail: World Bank · Financing agreement concluded, release of 11 November 2025 · five-year program · includes US$30 million of concessional financing from the Climate Investment Funds
register.note: Guarantee agreements for STEG under IBRD and Clean Technology Fund financing were referred to Parliament on 22 June 2026
register.text: Supports renewable energy deployment, the performance of the national electricity utility STEG, energy efficiency and the governance of the sector. The release cites the aim to add 2.8 gigawatts of new solar and wind capacity by 2028 and to create over 30,000 jobs; it serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Tataouine solar and battery storage
register.detail: EBRD · Approved by the Board 22 July 2026 · sovereign-guaranteed loans to STEG · tenor up to 18 years · Beni Mhira, Governorate of Tataouine
register.note: EBRD loan of up to €30 million and a €20 million concessional loan from the Clean Technology Fund; signature reported in November 2026
register.text: Finances a 50 MWac solar photovoltaic plant with a 10 MW / 20 MWh battery storage system, built for the national utility STEG in southern Tunisia. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Highway Network Extension Project to the El Kef and Jendouba regions
register.detail: IsDB · Approved at the 368th meeting of the Board of Executive Directors · release of 29 September 2026
register.note: One of six member countries in a US$938 million approval
register.text: Extends the motorway network to the El Kef and Jendouba regions, to promote economic integration and regional development through improved accessibility and connectivity. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Technical and energy efficiency of the Greater Tunis drinking water network
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved by the Board, release of 25 November 2025 · guarantee agreement signed in Tunis, 22 September 2026 · SONEDE
register.note: About 150 km of water pipes renewed, in a zone of nearly 2.7 million people
register.text: Modernises and strengthens the technical and energy performance of the drinking water network of Greater Tunis, run by SONEDE, starting with the renewal of about 150 km of pipes to cut losses. It serves the water standard for nearly 2.7 million people.

register.name: Environmental upgrading and rehabilitation of the Tunisian Chemical Group (PAER-GCT)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved by the Board 28 January 2026 · guarantee agreement signed in Tunis, 22 September 2026 · Gabès, Skhira and M’Dhilla
register.note: Signed with the Greater Tunis water financing: more than TND 698 million together
register.text: Finances the environmental upgrading of the Tunisian Chemical Group’s plants in Gabès, Skhira and M’Dhilla, to reduce air pollution sustainably and improve their environmental, energy and operational performance. It serves the health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Afreximbank second additional financing
register.detail: Afreximbank · Amendment No. 2 to the loan contract, 15 June 2026 · approved by Law No. 20 of 30 July 2026 · Central Bank of Tunisia, for the State
register.note: Adopted by Parliament on 29 July 2026; published in the Official Gazette No. 78 of 31 July 2026
register.text: A second additional financing of US$500 million from the African Export-Import Bank, contracted by the Central Bank of Tunisia on behalf of the State. It finances part of the state budget for 2026.

register.name: Murabaha financing for the Tunisian Chemical Group’s fertiliser inputs
register.detail: ITFC · two murabaha agreements guaranteed by the State, 1 and 2 December 2025 · approved by Parliament 29 July 2026 · up to 12 months for each drawdown
register.note: US$70 million and US$50 million; the second approved by Law No. 19 of 30 July 2026
register.text: Short-term Islamic trade finance for the Tunisian Chemical Group to secure sulphur and ammonia, the raw materials of its fertilisers, guaranteed by the Republic of Tunisia. Fertiliser for farms serves the food standard.

register.name: Gafsa Phosphate Company investment programme (CAPSA)
register.detail: EBRD · State guarantee agreement of 3 November 2025 · approved by Parliament 28 July 2026 · 10 years, with 3 years’ grace
register.note: With a €7 million technical grant; water reuse to rise from 60% to 90%
register.text: A state-guaranteed EBRD loan to the Gafsa Phosphate Company for modern drilling and haulage equipment and an advanced high-pressure filtration unit to treat wastewater, raising extraction capacity by about 30%. It serves the livelihood standard in the mining basin and saves water through reuse.

register.name: Afreximbank term loan
register.detail: Afreximbank · Approved by decree 8 June 2026 · Signed June 2026
register.note: Contracted by the Central Bank of Tunisia for the Ministry of Finance
register.text: A term loan from the African Export-Import Bank to the Central Bank of Tunisia for the Ministry of Finance. It is budget support within the 2026 budget law.

register.name: Renewal and development of the phosphate rail lines
register.detail: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development · loan agreement of 16 October 2025 · approved by Parliament 21 April 2026 · fixed rate 3.75%, 30 years with 4 years’ grace
register.note: 190.5 km of track renewed and a concrete sleeper factory; total cost $165.5 million
register.text: A loan to the Republic of Tunisia to renew and develop the rail lines that carry phosphate, including civil works on 190.5 km of track and a factory for concrete sleepers. It serves the livelihood standard in the mining regions.
by: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development

register.name: EU grants for solar grid connections, Sidi Bouzid and Gafsa
register.detail: European Union · Neighbourhood Investment Platform · release of 16 January 2026 · €20.4 million through the EBRD and €15.4 million through EIB Global · Global Gateway
register.note: For a 100 MW solar plant in Sidi Bouzid (Scatec and Aeolus) and a 300 MW solar portfolio in Gafsa (Qair)
register.text: EU grants that make large-scale renewable energy projects more bankable and support investment in grid connections and transmission infrastructure. Together the two projects total 400 MW of solar power, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: ELMED technical assistance grant for STEG
register.detail: European Union, through the EIB · signed in Tunis, release of 3 October 2025 · about TND 41 million
register.note: Expertise for STEG to oversee and manage the ELMED interconnector
register.text: An EU technical assistance grant, through the European Investment Bank, that finances the expertise STEG needs to oversee and manage ELMED, the undersea power link to Italy. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Youth and Women MSMEs and Entrepreneurship Support Project (YWESP)
register.detail: IsDB · Approved at the 358th meeting of the Board of Executive Directors, 15 December 2024 · blended line of financing
register.note: Especially for micro, small and medium enterprises in agri-food systems
register.text: A blended line of financing to create jobs for young women and men and to improve access to affordable finance for micro, small and medium enterprises, especially in agri-food systems. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: ELMED Tunisia–Italy electricity interconnector
register.detail: Team Europe · CEF grant agreement signed 7 August 2023 · €125 million of EBRD, EIB and KfW loans signed December 2023 · co-implemented by STEG and TERNA · operational in 2028
register.note: Team Europe mobilises €472.6 million, including €334.6 million of EU grants, for a project shared by Tunisia and Italy; the share of Tunisia is not stated
register.text: A 600 MW undersea power link between Tunisia and Italy, under construction and set to become operational in 2028. EU grants from the Connecting Europe Facility and loans for the undersea cable finance it; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Gafsa-Khobna Solar
register.detail: EIB · Approved 15 July 2026 · promoter Qair International · total cost about €235 million
register.note: About 120 MWp in Gafsa and about 237 MWp at Khobna, Sidi Bouzid
register.text: EIB finance for two solar photovoltaic plants developed by Qair: about 120 MWp in the Gafsa governorate and about 237 MWp at Khobna in the Sidi Bouzid governorate, with overhead lines to the grid. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Sidi Bouzid solar plant, Scatec and Aeolus
register.detail: EBRD and EIB · EIB approval 19 November 2025, signature 17 June 2026 · Scatec Khobna PV Power · EU grant of €5.5 million for transmission
register.note: EIB signed €33.15 million, including €2.5 million of investment grants
register.text: A loan package to the Scatec-Aeolus joint venture for a 100 MW solar photovoltaic plant in the Sidi Bouzid region, a large privately financed renewable energy project expected to generate an average of 252 GWh of electricity a year. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Enda Tamweel, Youth in Business loan
register.detail: EBRD · Approved 17 June 2025 · Youth in Business programme · supported by the EU through EFSD+
register.note: About €4.5 million, for businesses owned or led by entrepreneurs under 35
register.text: A loan of up to TND 15 million to Enda Tamweel, the country’s oldest and largest microfinance institution, for micro, small and medium enterprises owned or led by entrepreneurs under the age of 35. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Six tenths of the land in agriculture: olive groves, cereals and dates.

items.name: The Grid
items.label: Of citizens with electricity, 2024
items.text: Every household connected and every kitchen on clean fuel: a base for sun and wind to export power north.

items.name: The Schools
items.label: Complete lower secondary school, 2021
items.text: One of the most educated workforces in Africa, ready for industry and services.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 23.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Seabex
items.text: An agritech company whose AI-based, sensorless platform gives farmers precise irrigation recommendations, at work in Tunisia and France. It manages over 50,000 hectares, saving an average of 30% in water use.

items.name: Kumulus Water
items.text: Designs and manufactures atmospheric water generators that extract safe drinking water from air humidity, in use in schools, hotels and remote communities. It raised $3.5 million in seed funding in 2025 to scale operations in Tunisia, France and Spain.

items.name: GoMyCode
items.text: An edtech company that trains young people in new technologies, especially coding, to help them find a job. With the DROSOS Foundation it works with young Tunisian graduates from disadvantaged backgrounds in Sousse and the interior regions, where their unemployment rate is 50%.

items.name: AMEA Power
items.text: An independent power producer that commissioned a 120 MWp solar plant in Kairouan Governorate in December 2025, the largest solar plant in the nation.

items.name: Cure Bionics
items.text: A Tunisian company producing smart, CE-certified bionic hands, with 3D-printed sockets that clinicians scan, fit and print on site, financed by direct sales, training subscriptions and international grants. Between 2023 and 2025 more than 50 users were fitted and over 150 clinicians trained.

items.name: Enda Tamweel
items.text: A microfinance institution whose mission is to meet the microcredit needs of people with very low or no income, supporting the most vulnerable, notably women, young people and the rural population. It had more than 502,000 active clients at the end of 2024.
